newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada grain body cuts allowable barley moisture.
newsitem.headline: Canada grain body cuts allowable barley moisture.

text.p: The Canadian Grain Commission on Friday said it will cut the level of moisture it will accept in malting barley trans-shipments to 13.5 percent from 14 percent effective August 1, 1997.
Significant respiration occurs in malting barley during storage which reduces germination vigor and high moisture levels contribute to the process.

Storing and shipping barley at 13.5 percent moisture level reduces the chance a maltster or exporter will reject farmers' shipments due to poor germination vigor, a CGC statement said. The change was in response to exporter and maltster requests.
